source: Emergence of Cholera in the Central African Republic Germani 1998
processing_notes: Validated zero-transmission period 1999-2003 based on: (1) Germani 1998 documents cholera emergence in 1997 with no subsequent outbreak reports until 2004; (2) CDC EID 2021 confirms only 4 outbreaks in 1997-2016 with none between 1998-2003; (3) JHU database shows 22 cases in 1998 then 320 cases in 2004 with no intervening data. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence from comprehensive academic and WHO surveillance review. Surveillance system status: limited but functional with Institut Pasteur Bangui operational.

source: Seventh Pandemic Vibrio cholerae O1 Sublineages Central African Republic PMC
processing_notes: Validated zero-transmission period 2007-2010 based on: (1) CDC EID 2021 confirms only 4 outbreaks in 1997-2016 with none between 2006-2011; (2) UNICEF 2011 statement 'Because CAR has not had cholera cases in many years people do not necessarily know what basic measures to take' confirms extended absence prior to 2011; (3) WHO annual reports show 0 cases in 2005 and 2006 and no reports for 2007-2010. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence from multiple independent sources. Surveillance system status: disrupted but Institut Pasteur Bangui operational.

source: ReliefWeb Central African Republic Cholera Outbreak October 2011
processing_notes: Source states: 'government declared an epidemic on 30 September 2011, with 51 cases and 11 deaths registered' and 'New cases of cholera continued to be registered until the middle of October, when the total number of cases stood at 172 and the number of deaths was 16.' Interpreted as 172 sCh cases and 16 deaths for the complete 2011 outbreak. More precise temporal resolution (September-October 2011) than JHU annual aggregate (116 cases 15 deaths for full year 2011). The discrepancy between 172 (outbreak total per ReliefWeb/EID) and 116 (JHU annual) may reflect different surveillance periods or reporting definitions.

source: ReliefWeb Central African Republic Cholera Outbreak August 2016
processing_notes: Source states: 'From 27 July to 5 August 2016 at least 36 cases of acute watery diarrhea with severe dehydration were reported' and final count was '265 cholera cases including 139 children under 15 years old with some 20 deaths (lethality rate: 7.5%)' with end declared January 4 2017. Interpreted as 265 sCh cases and 20 deaths for complete 2016 outbreak. National total - includes Kemo Prefecture origin and spread to Bangui; do not double-count with any provincial-level JHU entries for same period.

source: UNICEF Central African Republic 2016 Cholera Outbreak Response
